environment: QEMU virt/HVF ARM64, 2 vCPU, 3 GiB, external Debian kernel/initramfs/modules; NOT Raspberry Pi boot
scope: A pristine dev9 copy received only the test observer, VT decoder and external-kernel module tree. The compressed release artifact was never booted or modified. A newly created dedicated 2 GiB qcow2 disk with serial JV_IMAGE_DATA_01 was the only formatted disk.
remote_rpc_assertions: Owner-authenticated preview/apply enabled the persistent reviewed setting
A real Tor SOCKS connection reached the product RPC v3 onion and authenticated Core 31.1 regtest RPC
Anonymous RPC returned 401 and /login returned 404 through the onion-only RPC listener
The TUI displayed committed/running/no-recovery state and the RPC onion
The same committed state and real onion RPC worked after an actual reboot
quick_connect_assertions: The actual browser WebSocket TUI created a second client and required explicit Q before rendering
The terminal matrix exactly matched the packaged Fully Noded btcrpc URI generator
All rendered QR cells used black/white terminal colors and neither captured client password remained visible
data_helper_assertions: Core 31.1 watch-only regtest block 1 and electrs height 1
Assigned wallet private_keys_enabled=false, descriptor import, PSBT creation and coin-control routes
Trusted-device LAN TLS Electrum header on port 50002 on both boots
Same registered volume UUID, watch-only wallet, chain height and service state after reboot

observer_failures_retained.cause: The observer made its first onion request before Tor completed circuit startup and timed out. The actual request criterion was retained and a bounded retry was added.
The observer evaluated a partially delivered terminal frame before the complete remote status arrived. The title, status and onion are now awaited together.
Back-to-back Escape keys were consumed by the preceding popup/menu. Each actual TUI transition is now awaited before sending the next key.

limits: The observer and its private checkpoint exist only in disposable mode-0600 copies and must never be distributed
The test used an external Debian kernel and did not exercise Raspberry Pi firmware, EEPROM, HAT storage or physical media
No installed Fully Noded or Nunchuk phone, physical camera, separate LAN client, hardware signer or 24-hour soak was tested
This is a development image and is unsigned
